source.text: ወርኢኩ፡ እምድኅረዝ፡ አእላፈ፡ አእላፍ፡ ወትእልፊተ፡ ትእልፊት፡ *ኍልቈ፡ ወኃሳበ፡ አልቦሙ፡ እለ፡ ይቀውሙ፡ ቅድመ፡ እግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት።
source.note: Actual Charles1906 selected print collated at full-page and native resolution. Printed stars and dagger boundaries retained; apparatus superscripts suppressed and punctuation normalized. Source text is the selected critical edition, not asserted unanimous manuscript wording. Author holds and interpretations are separately recorded; no later English oracle supplies this proposal.

translation.text: After that I saw thousands of thousands and tens of thousands of tens of thousands, beyond numbering or reckoning, standing before the Lord of Spirits.

source.text: ርኢኩ፡ ወበ*አርባዕቱ፡ ክነፊሁ፡ ለእግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት፡ ርኢኩ፡ አርባዕተ፡ *ገጸ፡ ካልአ፡ እምነ፡ እለ፡ ኢይነውሙ፡ ወአስማቲሆሙ፡ አእመርኩ፡ ዘአይድዐኒ፡ አስማቲሆሙ፡ መልአክ፡ ዘመጽአ፡ ምስሌየ፡ ወኵሎ፡ ኅቡኣተ፡ አርአየኒ።
source.note: Actual Charles1906 selected print collated at full-page and native resolution. Printed stars and dagger boundaries retained; apparatus superscripts suppressed and punctuation normalized. Source text is the selected critical edition, not asserted unanimous manuscript wording. Author holds and interpretations are separately recorded; no later English oracle supplies this proposal.

translation.text: I saw—at the four wings of the Lord of Spirits I saw four other faces,[a] different from those who do not sleep. I learned their names: the angel who came with me and showed me all the hidden things made their names known to me.

footnotes.text: The concrete word is “wings,” which can also refer to extremities or sides. “Faces” is retained as the visionary description rather than silently replaced with “beings.” The repeated “I saw” follows the selected text; Charles notes that some witnesses attach the opening occurrence to the preceding sentence.

source.text: ወሰማዕኩ፡ ቃሎሙ፡ ለ*እልኩ፡ ገጽ፡ አርባዕቱ፡ እንዘ፡ ይሴብሑ፡ ቅድመ፡ እግዚአ፡ ስብሐት።
source.note: Actual Charles1906 selected print collated at full-page and native resolution. Printed stars and dagger boundaries retained; apparatus superscripts suppressed and punctuation normalized. Source text is the selected critical edition, not asserted unanimous manuscript wording. Author holds and interpretations are separately recorded; no later English oracle supplies this proposal.

translation.text: I heard the voices of those four faces as they praised before the Lord of glory.

source.text: ቃለ፡ ቀዳማዊ፡ ይባርኮ፡ ለእግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት፡ ለዓለመ፡ ዓለም።
source.note: Actual Charles1906 selected print collated at full-page and native resolution. Printed stars and dagger boundaries retained; apparatus superscripts suppressed and punctuation normalized. Source text is the selected critical edition, not asserted unanimous manuscript wording. Author holds and interpretations are separately recorded; no later English oracle supplies this proposal.

translation.text: The first voice blesses the Lord of Spirits forever and ever.

source.text: ወ*ቃለ፡ ካልእ፡ ሰማዕኩ፡ እንዘ፡ ይባርኩ፡ ለ*ኅሩይ፡ ወለኅሩያን፡ እለ፡ ስቁላን፡ በእግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት።
source.note: Actual Charles1906 selected print collated at full-page and native resolution. Printed stars and dagger boundaries retained; apparatus superscripts suppressed and punctuation normalized. Source text is the selected critical edition, not asserted unanimous manuscript wording. Author holds and interpretations are separately recorded; no later English oracle supplies this proposal.

translation.text: I heard another voice blessing the Chosen One and the chosen ones who cling to the Lord of Spirits.[a]

footnotes.text: The participle can mean suspended or hanging upon, and by extension attached to or dependent upon someone. “Cling to” follows this attachment sense; the verse does not say that these chosen ones were crucified.

source.text: ወ*ሣልስ፡ ቃለ፡ ሰማዕኩ፡ *እንዘ፡ ይስእሉ፡ ወይጼሊ፡ በእንተ፡ እለ፡ የሐድሩ፡ ውስተ፡ የብስ፡ ወያስተበቍዑ፡ በስሙ፡ ለእግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት።
source.note: Actual Charles1906 selected print collated at full-page and native resolution. Printed stars and dagger boundaries retained; apparatus superscripts suppressed and punctuation normalized. Source text is the selected critical edition, not asserted unanimous manuscript wording. Author holds and interpretations are separately recorded; no later English oracle supplies this proposal.

translation.text: I heard the third voice asking and praying for those who dwell on dry land, and making entreaty in the name of the Lord of Spirits.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected asking, praying and entreating clauses have uneven singular/plural forms. Charles explicitly labels the asking/praying expression and the final entreating form as emendations in printed page81 notes6 and8. This rendering relates the entreaty to the third voice; the final plural expression can also be connected with the dwellers just mentioned. It is a rendering of the selected edited text, not a claim that every manuscript has this wording.

source.text: ወ*ቃለ፡ ራብዕ፡ ሰማዕኩ፡ እንዘ፡ ይሰድዶሙ፡ ለሰይጣናት፡ ወኢ*ይኀድግዎሙ፡ ይባኡ፡ ኀበ፡ እግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት፡ ከመ፡ ያስተዋድይዎሙ፡ ለእለ፡ የኃድሩ፡ ዲበ፡ የብስ።
source.note: Actual Charles1906 selected print collated at full-page and native resolution. Printed stars and dagger boundaries retained; apparatus superscripts suppressed and punctuation normalized. Source text is the selected critical edition, not asserted unanimous manuscript wording. Author holds and interpretations are separately recorded; no later English oracle supplies this proposal.

translation.text: I heard the fourth voice driving away the satans[a] and not allowing them to enter before the Lord of Spirits to accuse those who dwell on dry land.

footnotes.text: The selected word is plural. It designates accusing adversaries, “satans,” not a single named figure. The negative is retained: they are not permitted to enter and accuse the earth’s inhabitants.

source.text: ወእምድኅረዝ፡ ተስእልክዎ፡ ለመልአከ፡ ሰላም፡ ዘ*ምስሌየ፡ የሐውር፡ ዘውእቱ፡ አርአየኒ፡ ኵሎ፡ ዘኅቡእ፡ መኑ፡ ውእቶሙ፡ እሉ፡ ፬ገጽ፡ ዘርኢኩ፡ ወዘሰማዕኩ፡ ቃሎሙ፡ ወጸሐፍክዎሙ።
source.note: Actual Charles1906 selected print collated at full-page and native resolution. Printed stars and dagger boundaries retained; apparatus superscripts suppressed and punctuation normalized. Source text is the selected critical edition, not asserted unanimous manuscript wording. Author holds and interpretations are separately recorded; no later English oracle supplies this proposal.

translation.text: After that I asked the angel of peace, who travelled with me and showed me everything hidden, “Who are these four faces whom I saw, whose voices I heard and whom I wrote down?”

source.text: ወይቤለኒ፡ ዝቀዳማዊ፡ ውእቱ፡ መሓሪ፡ ወርሑቀ፡ መዓት፡ ሚካኤል፡ ካልእ፡ ዘዲበ፡ ኵሉ፡ *ሕማም፡ ወዲበ፡ ኵሉ፡ ቍስለ፡ ውሉደ፡ ሰብእ፡ ውእቱ፡ ሩፋኤል፡ ወሣልስ፡ ዘዲበ፡ ኵሉ፡ ኃይል፡ ውእቱ፡ ገብርኤል፡ ወራብዕ፡ ዘዲበ፡ *ንስሓ፡ ለተስፋ፡ እለ፡ ይወርሱ፡ ሕይወተ፡ ዘለዓለም፡ ዘስሙ፡ ፋኑኤል።
source.note: Actual Charles1906 selected print collated at full-page and native resolution. Printed stars and dagger boundaries retained; apparatus superscripts suppressed and punctuation normalized. Source text is the selected critical edition, not asserted unanimous manuscript wording. Author holds and interpretations are separately recorded; no later English oracle supplies this proposal.

translation.text: He told me, “This first one is Mikael, merciful and slow to anger. The second, who is over every illness and every wound of humankind, is Rufael. The third, who is over all power, is Gebriel. The fourth, who is over repentance for the hope of those who will inherit eternal life, is named Fanuel.”[a]

footnotes.text: Mikael, Rufael, Gebriel and Fanuel follow the selected Ethiopic name forms rather than silently substituting their more familiar English spellings. The fourth figure is linked with repentance and hope; the text does not explicitly name a separate office beyond the relation stated here.

source.text: ወእሉ፡ አርባዕቱ፡ መላእክቲሁ፡ ለ*እግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት፡ ወአርባዕተ፡ ቃለ፡ ሰማዕኩ፡ በውእቱኒ፡ መዋዕል።
source.note: Actual Charles1906 selected print collated at full-page and native resolution. Printed stars and dagger boundaries retained; apparatus superscripts suppressed and punctuation normalized. Source text is the selected critical edition, not asserted unanimous manuscript wording. Author holds and interpretations are separately recorded; no later English oracle supplies this proposal.

translation.text: These are the four angels of the Lord of Spirits, and I heard four voices in those days.

source.text: ወእምድኅረዝ፡ ርኢኩ፡ ኵሎ፡ *ኅቡኣቲሁ፡ ለሰማያት፡ ወመንግሥተ፡ እፎ፡ ትትካፈል፡ ወትግባረ፡ ሰብእ፡ ከመ፡ በመዳልው፡ ይደለው።
source.note: Actual Charles1906 selected print collated at full-page and native resolution. Printed stars and dagger boundaries retained; apparatus superscripts suppressed and punctuation normalized. Source text is the selected critical edition, not asserted unanimous manuscript wording. Author holds and interpretations are separately recorded; no later English oracle supplies this proposal.

translation.text: After that I saw all the hidden things of the heavens, how the kingdom is divided, and how the works of humankind are weighed in a balance.

source.text: በህየ፡ ርኢኩ፡ መኃድሪሆሙ፡ ለኃጥኣን፡ ወ*መኃድሪሆሙ፡ ለቅዱሳን፡ ወርእያ፡ አዕይንትየ፡ በህየ፡ ኵሎሙ፡ ኃጥኣን፡ እንዘ፡ ይሰደዱ፡ እምህየ፡ እለ፡ ይክሕድዎ፡ ለ*ስመ፡ እግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት፡ ወ*ይስሐቡ፡ ወ*ቀዊመ፡ አልቦሙ፡ በመቅሠፍት፡ እንተ፡ ትወጽእ፡ እምእግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት።
source.note: Actual Charles1906 selected print collated at full-page and native resolution. Printed stars and dagger boundaries retained; apparatus superscripts suppressed and punctuation normalized. Source text is the selected critical edition, not asserted unanimous manuscript wording. Author holds and interpretations are separately recorded; no later English oracle supplies this proposal.

translation.text: There I saw the dwellings of sinners and the dwellings of the holy ones. My eyes saw there all the sinners who deny the name of the Lord of Spirits being driven away from that place. They are dragged away and cannot stand under the scourge that comes from the Lord of Spirits.

source.text: ወበህየ፡ ርእያ፡ አዕይንትየ፡ ኅቡኣተ፡ መብረቅት፡ ወነጐድጓድ፡ ወ*ኅቡኣተ፡ ነፋሳት፡ እፎ፡ ይትከፈሉ፡ ከመ፡ ይንፍሑ፡ ዲበ፡ ምድር፡ ወኅቡኣተ፡ ደመናት፡ ወጠል፡ ወበህየ፡ ርኢኩ፡ እምኀበ፡ ይመጽእ፡ በውእቱ፡ መካን፡ ወ*እምህየ፡ ይጸግቡ፡ ጸበለ፡ ምድር።
source.note: Actual Charles1906 selected print collated at full-page and native resolution. Printed stars and dagger boundaries retained; apparatus superscripts suppressed and punctuation normalized. Source text is the selected critical edition, not asserted unanimous manuscript wording. Author holds and interpretations are separately recorded; no later English oracle supplies this proposal.

translation.text: There my eyes saw the hidden things of lightning and thunder, and the hidden things of the winds—how they are divided to blow upon the earth—and the hidden things of clouds and dew. There I saw where it comes from in that place; from there they are filled with the dust of the earth.[a]

footnotes.text: The final verb is read in its basic “be sated/filled” sense, with the dust expression as an accusative complement. Dillmann’s1865 lexicon, column1315, permits this construction and inanimate subjects. The identity of “they” and the imagery remain difficult. “They saturate the dust” would instead give the clause an active, causative sense, which is not silently substituted here. The preceding “how” is እፎ, not an assertion about the winds’ mouths.

source.text: በህየ፡ ርኢኩ፡ መዛግብተ፡ ዕፁው፡ ወእምኔሆሙ፡ ይትከፈሉ፡ ነፋስ፡ መዝገበ፡ *በረድ፡ ወነፋስ፡ መዝገበ፡ ጊሜ፡ *ወዘደመና፡ ወደመና፡ ዚአሁ፡ እምላዕለ፡ ምድር፡ የኀድር፡ እምቅድመ፡ ዓለም።
source.note: Actual Charles1906 selected print collated at full-page and native resolution. Printed stars and dagger boundaries retained; apparatus superscripts suppressed and punctuation normalized. Source text is the selected critical edition, not asserted unanimous manuscript wording. Author holds and interpretations are separately recorded; no later English oracle supplies this proposal.

translation.text: There I saw closed storehouses. From them the winds are apportioned: the wind from the storehouse of hail, the wind from the storehouse of mist, and that of the cloud; its cloud dwells above the earth from before the world.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected text says that the storehouses are closed, not that they are storehouses of lightning. The list repeats “wind” and “storehouse,” and then repeats “cloud”; the precise relation of these compressed expressions is awkward. “From” in the list expresses the provisional storehouse/wind relation, not an extra printed preposition. The weather word rendered “mist” also belongs to the fog/cloud semantic range.

source.text: ወርኢኩ፡ መዛግብተ፡ ፀሐይ፡ ወዘወርኅ፡ እምአይቴ፡ ይወፅኡ፡ ወአይቴ፡ ይገብኡ፡ ወግብኦቶሙ፡ ስቡሕ፡ ወእፎ፡ ይከብር፡ አሐዱ፡ ለካልኡ፡ ወምሕዋሮሙ፡ ብፁዕ፡ ወኢ*የኃልፉ፡ ምሕዋረ፡ ወኢይዌስኩ፡ ወኢያኃጽጹ፡ እምሕዋረ፡ ዚአሆሙ፡ ወሃይማኖተ፡ የዐቅቡ፡ አሐዱ፡ ምስለ፡ ካልኡ፡ በመሐላ፡ †ዘ*ኃደሩ†።
source.note: Actual Charles1906 selected print collated at full-page and native resolution. Printed stars and dagger boundaries retained; apparatus superscripts suppressed and punctuation normalized. Source text is the selected critical edition, not asserted unanimous manuscript wording. Author holds and interpretations are separately recorded; no later English oracle supplies this proposal.

translation.text: I saw the storehouses of the sun and moon: where they come out and where they go in, their glorious return, and how one surpasses the other in glory. Their course is blessed. They do not overstep their course, add to it or take away from their course. They keep faith with one another by an oath—“who have dwelt.”[a]

footnotes.text: The complete unit continues onto printed page83. Charles encloses the final words, literally “who have dwelt,” with daggers and calls the text corrupt. His apparatus proposes how a wording about swearing could have become one about dwelling, but that conjecture is not silently substituted here. The quoted ending is provisional and is not a claim of a coherent recovered clause.

source.text: ወይወፅእ፡ ቅድመ፡ ፀሐይ፡ ወይገብር፡ ፍኖቶ፡ በትእዛዘ፡ እግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት፡ ወይጸንዕ፡ ስሙ፡ ለዓለመ፡ ዓለም።
source.note: Actual Charles1906 selected print collated at full-page and native resolution. Printed stars and dagger boundaries retained; apparatus superscripts suppressed and punctuation normalized. Source text is the selected critical edition, not asserted unanimous manuscript wording. Author holds and interpretations are separately recorded; no later English oracle supplies this proposal.

translation.text: The sun comes out first and makes its course at the command of the Lord of Spirits, and his name endures forever and ever.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected verb says that the name is firm or endures; it does not say that the sun praises the name. “His” is retained without resolving its reference into a newly supplied noun.

source.text: ወእምድኅረ*ዝ፡ ርኢኩ፡ ፍኖተ፡ ዘኅቡእ፡ ወክሡት፡ ዘወርኅ፡ ወምሕዋረ፡ ፍኖቱ፡ ይፌጽም፡ በውእቱ፡ መካን፡ በመዐልት፡ ወበሌሊት፡ ወአሐዱ፡ ለካልኡ፡ ይኔጽር፡ በቅድመ፡ *እግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት፡ ወየአኵቱ፡ ወይሴብሑ፡ ወኢየዐርፉ፡ እስመ፡ አኵቴቶሙ፡ ዕረፍት፡ ውእቱ፡ ሎሙ።
source.note: Actual Charles1906 selected print collated at full-page and native resolution. Printed stars and dagger boundaries retained; apparatus superscripts suppressed and punctuation normalized. Source text is the selected critical edition, not asserted unanimous manuscript wording. Author holds and interpretations are separately recorded; no later English oracle supplies this proposal.

translation.text: After that I saw the hidden and visible path of the moon. It completes the course of its path in that place by day and by night. One looks toward the other before the Lord of Spirits.[a] They give thanks and praise and do not rest, because their thanksgiving is rest for them.

footnotes.text: Charles printed page83 note8 reports that most of the manuscripts he cites omit the unstarred “I saw” verb, though he regards such a verb as required by the context and by the wording discussed in note9. Note9 concerns the following “path”; neither note is attached to the later unstarred “it completes” verb. The singular and plural shifts are retained rather than made into a new speech by a named angel. “One ... the other” leaves the two referents implicit.

source.text: እስመ፡ ፀሐይ፡ ብዙኅ፡ መያጢ፡ ቦቱ፡ *ለበረከት፡ ወለመረገም፡ ወምርዋጸ፡ ፍኖቱ፡ ለወርኅ፡ ለጻድቃን፡ ብርሃን፡ ወለኃጥኣን፡ ጽልመት፡ በስሙ፡ ለእግዚአ፡ ዘፈጠረ፡ ማእከለ፡ ብርሃን፡ ወማእከለ፡ ጽልመት፡ ወከፈለ፡ መንፈሶሙ፡ ለሰብእ፡ ወአጽንዐ፡ መንፈሶሙ፡ ለጻድቃን፡ በስመ፡ ጽድቅ፡ ዚአሁ።

translation.text: The sun has many changes for blessing and for cursing, and the course of the moon’s path is light for the righteous and darkness for sinners. This is in the name of the Lord, who created the midst of light and the midst of darkness,[a] divided their spirit among humankind, and strengthened their spirit for the righteous in the name of his righteousness.[b]

footnotes.text: The selected construction combines “created” with two expressions for “midst/between.” The provisional English preserves this awkward construction. It has not been silently replaced by “divided light from darkness”; the precise construction still needs grammatical adjudication.

The expression “their spirit,” with a plural possessive suffix, occurs twice. Its antecedents and the relation between the spirit assigned to humankind and that strengthened for the righteous are not fully explicit; the text is not harmonized into a different cosmology.

source.text: እስመ፡ መልአክ፡ ኢይክል፡ ወስልጣን፡ ኢይክል፡ ከሊአ፡ እስመ፡ ለመኰንን፡ ለኵሎሙ፡ ይሬኢ፡ ወ*እሉንቱ፡ ኵሎሙ፡ በቅድሜሁ፡ ውእቱ፡ ይኴንን።

translation.text: No angel can prevent it, nor can any ruler: he sees them all for judgment, and he himself judges all these before him.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected text has “sees ... for judgment.” Charles records a different construction in most manuscripts which, together with another verb, would produce a wording about appointing a judge. The rendering here follows the selected seeing verb instead of silently adopting that different text. The unexpressed object of “prevent” is supplied only as “it.”
